$ FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test  # transforms
    The root-package check for the module-root corpus runs in normal runs, so it runs after the update: go test ./...
    script/errs/transform/looped: looped declines the base: the base's do/ tree already errs
    script/garbled/transform/looped: looped declines the base: the base states malformed, which looped neither gives nor keeps
    script/garbled/transform/upper: upper declines the base: the base states malformed, which upper neither gives nor keeps

$ edit testdata/script/twice.txtar  # edit upper's input by hand
$ go test ./b  # tr-b
    no registry records a root-package check for the module-root corpus, so nothing reports what no column there owns.
        Register hypercase.RootPackage() in one package over it, then run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... to record it in the package's registry.
    script/errs/transform/looped: looped declines the base: the base's do/ tree already errs
    script/garbled/transform/looped: looped declines the base: the base states malformed, which looped neither gives nor keeps
    script/garbled/transform/upper: upper declines the base: the base states malformed, which upper neither gives nor keeps
    script/twice/transform/upper: Uppercases every file under do/out/.
        copy: Does what the case's do/ tree says.
        transform/upper/out/copy/values.txt differs (-golden +got):
        - A1 SIX
        + A1 SEVEN
        If the change is intended, run FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./... and read the diff before committing.
    script/twice/transform/upper: Uppercases every file under do/out/.
        A cell of the variant failed, and the archive's inputs for upper's variant differ from what upper makes now:
        transform/upper/in/do/out/values.txt differs (-committed +made):
        - A1 SEVEN
        + A1 SIX
        A normal run reads the inputs, and an update what upper makes. The module's update, FIXTURE_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test ./..., rewrites them, in the package that owns upper, and the variant's cells. If no package owns upper, the root-package check says so, and no update rewrites the inputs.
--- FAIL: TestCorpus
